Article Title: ‘Rural safety net under attack’: Jairam Ramesh calls MGNREGA replacement a ‘surgical strike’
Article Text:
Ramesh referred to drought conditions in Beed and other districts of Maharashtra

Jairam ramesh alleges wage theft, fake attendance

MGNREGA replaced by vb-g ram g act

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Tuesday called the replacement of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) with the VB-G RAM G Act a “surgical strike” on the social safety net protecting rural India, alleging that the move had weakened support for workers facing distress.In a post on X, Ramesh referred to drought conditions in Beed and other districts of Maharashtra, which he said were facing their worst drought in a decade. He said MGNREGA had provided a guarantee of support to rural workers during such crises, but alleged that its replacement had undermined that protection.“Beed and other districts in Maharashtra are facing the worst drought in a decade. MGNREGA was the guarantee of support in such times of extreme distress. But its replacement with VB-G RAM G is nothing less than a surgical strike on the social safety net that protected rural India,” he wrote.Ramesh also cited a field-level investigation published by a media outlet, alleging that villagers had not received work for months despite official records showing them as employed.He claimed that local politicians were pocketing workers’ wages and alleged that similar cases involving fake attendance and clone application scams had been reported in Uttar Pradesh and other BJP-ruled states.“This is not just corruption, but systemic theft of workers’ wages,” Ramesh said, accusing the government of presiding over what he called the theft of rural wages.The Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, or VB-G RAM G Act, came into effect on July 1 after being passed during Parliament’s Winter Session in 2025.The legislation replaced MGNREGA’s 100-day employment guarantee with a 125-day guarantee. However, the Opposition has criticised the new law over the removal of Mahatma Gandhi’s name from the scheme and the introduction of a 60:40 Centre-State funding arrangement.
Article Summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh called the replacement of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) with the VB-G RAM G Act a ‘surgical strike’ on the social safety net protecting rural India. He said the move had weakened support for workers facing distress. He claimed that local politicians were pocketing workers’ wages.

Article Title: 'No double standards on terrorism': Rajnath Singh's stern warning at SCO meet with Pakistan at the table
Article Text:
‘Entire terror ecosystem must be dismantled’: Rajnath Singh at SCO meet with Ishaq Dar present

Rajnath meets Tajik, Iranian leaders on SCO sidelines

What is on the SCO agenda?

NEW DELHI: With Pakistan’s deputy PM Ishaq Dar in the room, defence minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday delivered a strong message against terrorism at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) meeting in Tajikistan's Dushanbe.Addressing representatives of SCO member countries, Rajnath said terrorism remained one of the biggest threats to peace and development, warning that its impact extended far beyond the loss of innocent lives.“Terrorism not only causes the loss of innocent lives but also disrupts investment and commerce. It radicalises society and deprives our youth of the opportunities they deserve,” the defence minister said.The defence minister stressed that terrorism could not be justified under any circumstances and called for a united approach against those who enable it.“There should be no double standards in dealing with terrorism, and no place for those who finance, support or provide safe havens to terrorists. The entire ecosystem of terrorism must be firmly and collectively dismantled,” he said.Rajnath's remarks come days after he reiterated India’s firm position on crossborder terrorism, warning on October 15 that any further terrorist acts originating from Pakistan would invite an even stronger response.Speaking at the Times Network Defence Conclave in New Delhi, he said India’s commitment to dialogue, coexistence and peaceful dispute resolution should not be mistaken for weakness.“Operation Sindoor, Balakot Airstrikes and Surgical Strikes weren’t just military operations; they symbolised a decisive shift in the nation’s approach, moving from diplomatic condemnation to proactive action aimed at rooting out terrorism by reaching its very source,” Rajnath said.He also said that since 2014, the ‘shelf life’ of most terrorists had fallen to less than a year, with security forces neutralising them within a year of their taking up arms against India.Emphasising the link between strength and peace, Rajnath said India remained committed to peaceful coexistence while staying prepared to deal with threats to its security.“Our commitment to peace remains steadfast, yet we are fully prepared to confront any challenge. Our goal is to build an India that, while advocating for peace, remains vigilant when it comes to security and is fully capable of safeguarding its sovereignty, integrity, and national interests,” he said.On the sidelines of the SCO meeting, Singh held separate meetings with Tajikistan Prime Minister Qohir Rosulzoda and Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref.During his meeting with Rosulzoda, Singh highlighted the longstanding civilisational ties and close people-to-people connections between India and Tajikistan.In a post on X, the defence minister said, "Delighted to meet H.E. Mr Qohir Rosulzoda, Prime Minister of Tajikistan at the commencement of SCO Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe. Underlined the longstanding civilisational ties and deep people to people links between India and Tajikistan."Rajnath also met Aref and shared details of the interaction on X. "Pleasure to meet H.E. Mr Mohammad Reza Aref, First Vice President of Iran on the sidelines of the SCO Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe," he wrote.Rajnath is representing India at the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in the Tajik capital, where leaders and representatives of member countries have gathered to discuss regional cooperation.Ahead of the meeting, Tajikistan President Emomali Rahmon welcomed Singh and other representatives of SCO member countries at the Palace of the Nation in Dushanbe.According to the ministry of defence, the meeting will focus on strengthening cooperation in culture, connectivity, the economy, innovation, investment and people-to-people ties. Members will also review progress in the organisation's financial and institutional functioning.The ministry highlighted India's contributions across various SCO mechanisms, including initiatives in start-ups, digital public infrastructure and cultural exchanges, saying these offered opportunities to advance practical and mutually beneficial cooperation among member countries.
Article Summary: Rajnath Singh delivers a strong message against terrorism at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) meeting in Tajikistan's Dushanbe. He said terrorism remained one of the biggest threats to peace and development, warning that its impact extended far beyond the loss of innocent lives.

Article Title: 'Values that inspired Captain Smit Machchhar': RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat cites flydubai pilot in Vijayadashami speech
Article Text:
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat says Hindu values inspired Flydubai Captain Smit Machchhar’s courage to protect lives.

NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Tuesday linked Captain Smit Machchhar’s courage in preventing a possible plane disaster to Hindu values and traditions, saying these values inspire people to protect human lives and ensure the safety of others.Addressing the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh’s annual Vijayadashami celebrations at its headquarters in Nagpur, Bhagwat said Machchhar’s actions reflected values passed down through generations."Since the Hindu society's worldview and nature are inclusive, we must understand that such efforts will only strengthen the emotional unity, goodwill, and good conduct among all of us. It is this very nature and these values, passed down from generation to generation, that inspires Captain Smith Machchar to put his own life in danger and devote himself to protect human lives," Bhagwat said.Machchhar became widely praised after he fought off his co-pilot, who attacked him aboard a Flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv with 174 people on board. Despite sustaining stab wounds, the captain managed to resist the attack, allowing passengers and crew members to intervene and restrain the co-pilot.Bhagwat said the RSS was working to awaken the Hindu spirit and build a well-organised and strong society."RSS is working to awaken the Hindu spirit and build the entire society into a well-organized and strong society...It is these values that inspired Captain Smit Machchhar to do what he did..."He also said the actions of individuals guided by these values could strengthen national unity and promote harmony across communities."Driven by this very ethos, what Captain Smit Machchhar did recently was natural. There was no training on what to do in such a situation; her innate tradition and values simply surfaced during that moment of testing. This is the Hindu nature. Consequently, it naturally nurtures and protects the dignity and security of all diversity. This work serves as a constructive force for national unity and global harmony. And this is not something we merely talk about.People do not join the Sangh to listen to speeches; they come first and cultivate the practice of this ethos through their actions..."The RSS chief also spoke about national unity, describing the bond among Indians as unconditional and rooted in a sense of belonging and affection."The Unity of us Bharatiyas - Intrinsic and Unconditional The bond we share with one another and our relationship with Bharat are living bonds, rooted in the heart and therefore unconditional. They are one-sided in nature, as expressed in the words: 'May your glory remain eternal, O Mother; whether we live for a few more days or not'," Bhagwat said.He added that the freedom fighters had demonstrated complete devotion to the nation during the struggle against British rule."Our freedom fighters demonstrated this very spirit of complete and unconditional devotion to the nation. It was this devotion that ultimately compelled the British government to leave Bharat," Bhagwat said.
Article Summary: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh chief Mohan Bhagwat says Hindu values inspired Flydubai Captain Smit Machchhar’s courage to protect lives. He said the actions of individuals guided by these values could strengthen national unity and promote harmony across communities.

Article Title: 'Vote Chori Ki Raasleela’: Youth Congress burns Ravan effigy with Gyanesh's face - watch

NEW DELHI: The Indian Youth Congress (IYC) on Monday burned an effigy of Ravan bearing the face of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi, demanding his resignation over alleged irregularities in the Election Commission’s functioning and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The protest was held at the IYC headquarters on Raisina Road and featured a street performance titled Vote Chori Ki Raasleela, aimed at highlighting allegations of electoral manipulation and questioning the transparency and impartiality of the poll panel, according to a statement issued by the organisation.Addressing the gathering, IYC national president Uday Bhanu Chib said the protests would continue until Kumar resigned or was jailed.“Gyanesh Kumar, who is finishing off the democracy and Constitution of the country, cannot save himself. We will continue to protest in different forms. This will continue until he goes behind bars or resigns. He has indulged in ‘vote chori’. Until he is jailed, people of the country will continue to protest,” Chib told news agency ANI.Chib said the Election Commission must be accountable to the public and that the CEC should take moral responsibility for concerns raised over electoral transparency.“Democracy is not merely about holding elections; it is about ensuring that every vote is respected and every citizen's mandate is protected.“When serious questions are raised about electoral transparency, the responsibility of the Election Commission is to provide clear answers and uphold the highest standards of impartiality,” he said.In its statement, the IYC said the effigy-burning was intended to convey its opposition to alleged electoral irregularities and demand accountability from the poll panel.“Through our 'Vote Chori Ki Raasleela' protest, the Indian Youth Congress is sending a clear message that the youth of this country will not allow the sanctity of democracy to be compromised. The burning of the effigy of CEC Gyanesh Kumar represents our anger and our demand for accountability,” Chib said.The protest followed the launch of the IYC’s digital campaign, Digital Ravan Dahan, which invites citizens to identify what the organisation calls the “10 heads of India's Ravan”. According to the IYC, the campaign allows people to register their views through its website and is scheduled to culminate in a virtual Ravan Dahan on Tuesday at 7:30 pm.The IYC has been demanding Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Election Commission’s functioning and the SIR exercise. Opposition parties have also raised concerns about aspects of the electoral roll revision process.The organisation said it would continue its protests and public campaigns until its demands for greater electoral transparency and institutional accountability were addressed.
Article Summary: The Indian Youth Congress (IYC) burned an effigy of Ravan bearing the face of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi. The protest was held at the IYC headquarters on Raisina Road and featured a street performance titled Vote Chori Ki Raasleela. The IYC has been demanding Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities.

Article Title: Tiger Shroff shooting: The Salman Khan connection and a trail of threats linked to Lawrence Bishnoi

NEW DELHI: Gangster Lawrence Bishnoi 's long-running feud with Salman Khan brought actor Tiger Shroff into the spotlight on Sunday after gunmen opened fire at his car in Mumbai's Juhu. Seven rounds were fired in the incident, but the actor escaped without bullet injuries.Shroff's driver, Firdaus, and another person were injured in the October 18 attack, which prompted a police investigation into the identity of the assailants and their motive.A message attributed to the Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the firing and linked it to Shroff's association with superstar Salman Khan. The message also warned others in the film industry against working with Salman.The attack is the latest in a series of incidents involving threats and violence allegedly linked to the Bishnoi network against Bollywood personalities and others associated with Salman Khan.The Bishnoi gang's message after the incident linked the attack to Tiger Shroff's professional association with Salman Khan. It claimed that Shroff had been warned earlier but had ignored the warning.The message stated: "Anyone in the Mumbai film industry who does not listen to us or works with Salman Khan will be next."In an audio message released after the attack, a man identified as Anil Pandit threatened Salman Khan and his family, warning the actor against relying on his security and demanding an apology to Lawrence Bishnoi and the Bishnoi community."Listen to me carefully, Salman Khan. If you don't apologise to my elder brother, Lawrence Bishnoi, or to the Bishnoi community, then we won't even leave a dog in your house. We will destroy your entire family. Keep this in mind. Don't think that you are in security and nothing will happen to you," Pandit said in the audio message.The message also warned rival gang members against using the group's name to gain attention. It appeared to be aimed at intimidating not just Shroff but others in the film industry who work with Salman Khan.The authenticity of the messages and the gang's claimed role in the attack remain subject to police verification.The dispute involving the Bajrangi Bhaijaan actor dates back to the 1998 blackbuck poaching case. Lawrence Bishnoi has repeatedly threatened the actor over the case, citing the blackbuck's religious significance to the Bishnoi community.The threats against Salman Khan have continued for years.In June 2022, a threat letter was reportedly found at Bandra Bandstand, where the actor's father, Salim Khan, used to go for walks.The letter warned that Salman Khan would meet the same fate as Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala, who was murdered in May that year.In March 2023, Salman Khan's manager received a threatening email referring to Lawrence Bishnoi's threats against the actor. The email also mentioned Goldy Brar, a Canada-based gangster and a close associate of Lawrence Bishnoi.On April 14, 2024, two motorcycle-borne men opened fire outside Salman Khan's Galaxy Apartments residence in Bandra. The actor was not injured.Mumbai Police alleged that the shooting was carried out at the behest of the Bishnoi gang. Anmol Bishnoi, Lawrence's brother and a close associate, was among those wanted in connection with the case.Investigators examined the roles of the alleged shooters and their associates, including how the attack was planned.In a separate case, Navi Mumbai Police filed a chargesheet in 2024 alleging that members of the gang had been offered Rs 25 lakh to attack Salman Khan.According to the police, the plan included targeting him during a film shoot or while he was travelling to his Panvel farmhouse.The case also highlighted the role of people allegedly involved in surveillance and planning, beyond those who directly carried out an attack.The threats surrounding Salman drew further attention after former Maharashtra minister Baba Siddique was shot dead on October 12, 2024.Siddique, a three-time MLA and Nationalist Congress Party leader, was killed outside the office of his son, Zeeshan Siddique, in Bandra East.A social media post linked to the Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the murder and warned those helping Salman Khan. Police investigated the alleged links.On February 1, 2026, gunmen opened fire outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty's residence in Juhu.A post attributed to people linked to the Bishnoi network claimed responsibility and threatened further violence if its demands were ignored.Mumbai Police and the Crime Branch investigated the shooting, including the suspected attackers and their alleged links to the network.How the Bishnoi network operatesThe Lawrence Bishnoi network's alleged modus operandi involves different people handling the planning and execution of attacks.Police investigations have examined suspected surveillance, recruitment of shooters, weapons supply, communication between associates, and arrangements for transport and escape.In the 2024 case involving Salman, police alleged that the attackers had gathered information about the actor's movements and locations over an extended period. Investigators also looked into the roles of several people suspected of helping plan the attack.The network led by jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi has also been linked to attacks beyond India, including incidents in Canada and the UK.These include multiple shootings at comedian Kapil Sharma's cafe in Canada, which drew attention to the gang's overseas reach.In November 2025, news agency PTI reported that the National Investigation Agency arrested Anmol Bishnoi after his deportation from the United States.He was wanted in cases including the murder of Baba Siddique and the firing outside Salman Khan's residence.Anmol is Lawrence Bishnoi's brother and a close associate.Mumbai Police are investigating the firing to identify the attackers and establish the motive.Officers are examining CCTV footage and forensic evidence, while checking the authenticity of messages attributed to Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu.Investigators are also looking into whether Shroff had received any threats before the incident.The probe will need to establish whether the attackers acted on behalf of an organised group or whether someone claimed responsibility after the shooting to exploit the incident.For now, the alleged Bishnoi gang link remains under investigation.
Article Summary: Gangster Lawrence Bishnoi's long-running feud with Salman Khan brought actor Tiger Shroff into the spotlight on Sunday. Seven rounds were fired in the incident, but the actor escaped without bullet injuries. The attack is the latest in a series of incidents involving threats and violence allegedly linked to the Bish noi network against Bollywood personalities.

Article Title: 'State-sponsored terrorism': Mamata Banerjee demands release of CJP's Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee on Monday accused the government of perpetrating “state-sponsored terrorism” and “police-sponsored atrocities” as she demanded the release of Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. The CJP duos judicial custody was extended by two days in a case linked to the alleged trespassing at Jantar Mantar in Delhi.In a post on X, Banerjee alleged that the authorities were deliberately extending the duo's custody and accused those in power of using a “dangerous virus” to attack democracy. She also condemned the alleged treatment of young protesters, invoking India's freedom struggle to argue that people would continue to resist what she described as attacks on democratic rights.“I can understand the desperate motive to extend the custody of Ashutosh and Saurav. This is a dangerous virus being used on a daily basis to attack democracy. Stop torturing the boys and girls of Gen Z. Those in power today, will not be in power tomorrow,” she wrote.“From Kolkata to Delhi to Mumbai - throughout the country, atrocities have reached unprecedented levels,” Banerjee added.Drawing a parallel with the struggle against British colonial rule, the former chief minister said those who fought for India's independence had also faced atrocities but continued their fight with conviction.“When our forefathers stood up to colonial rulers, they too had to face atrocities and yet they fought with conviction and valor. Let me say it clearly: this is state-sponsored terrorism. These are police-sponsored atrocities. These cannot sustain for long,” she wrote.Banerjee further said that sustained public resistance would eventually force those in power to recognise the concerns of protesters.“When people with conviction keep standing up strongly for the cause, to Save India, to Save Democracy- only then will these arrogant and blindfolded politicians in government open their eyes. By that time the people would have won, and the murderers of democracy will be finished,” she said.The remarks came after a Special Executive Magistrate at Mandir Marg police station extended the judicial custody of Das and Ranka by two days on Monday. Delhi Police also transferred the trespassing case to its Crime Branch unit for further investigation, according to police sources cited by PTI.The two were sent to judicial custody on October 14 over allegations that they trespassed into private premises to reach Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a protest site a day earlier, and violated bonds requiring them to maintain peace.

NEW DELHI: Three Meitei villagers were killed and three others injured after unidentified armed militants opened fire on a group collecting firewood in Manipur on Monday, officials said. It triggered protests in Imphal, where locals placed two of the victims' bodies outside Manipur chief minister Y Khemchand Singh's residence.The attack took place around 9.40 am at Sunulok Hill, ahead of Khongbal in the Tangkhul area, under Sagolmang police station.It came amid a series of violent incidents since Sunday night, including a fatal shooting during a clash between two communities in Thoubal district and an improvised explosive device (IED) blast that seriously injured three CRPF personnel.Addressing the incidents, Manipur Police ADGP Lhari Dorjee Lhatoo said security forces had intensified operations and were investigating all three incidents."Police and security forces are taking the matter with utmost concern. Necessary security measures have been put in place and the situation is being very closely monitored," he said.The victims were part of a group of 14 Meitei villagers who had gone to cut and transport firewood when unidentified armed militants opened fire on them, Lhatoo said."Today at around 9:40 AM, unidentified armed militants opened fire on a group of 14 Meitei villagers who were engaged in cutting and transporting firewood ahead of Khongbal, Tangkhul area, the exact spot is Sunulok Hill under Sagolmang police station," he said."In the incident, three individuals succumbed to bullet injuries. Three other individuals have also sustained injuries. The injured have been safely evacuated and are undergoing further medical treatment," he added.The deceased were identified in an earlier account as Arubam Ronil, 35, Lairenlakpam Inaobi, 51, and Kshetrimayum Sushil, 32. Ronil and Inaobi died on the spot, while Sushil succumbed to his injuries at a private hospital in Imphal.The injured were identified as N Suraj, 19, Meisnam Somendro, 53, and K Bosan, 45. Three other people were reported missing in earlier accounts of the attack.An injured survivor told officials, "While we were loading the firewood, we were suddenly fired upon," according to news agency PTI.Police have received inputs about those involved and are investigating the attack. Lhatoo said, "Various inputs regarding the persons involved have already been received. The matter is under thorough investigation, and after due process, we will ensure all necessary action will be taken to punish the perpetrators of such heinous crimes."He said joint teams of police, CoBRAs, CRPF, Assam Rifles and BSF were conducting operations in the area."Even as we speak, operations are on in the area with joint teams of Police, CoBRAs, CRPF, Assam Rifles, and BSF, and more Int-based operations are in the offing on priority," he said."Sniffer dogs and drones are being used, and helicopter surveillance has also commenced," he added.Angry locals brought two of the deceased's bodies to Imphal and placed them outside the main gate of the chief minister's residence in Babupara to protest the continuing violence in the state.Police fired several rounds of tear gas shells to disperse the protesters. The bodies were subsequently taken to the Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Medical Sciences (JNIMS).Security was tightened around the chief minister's bungalow and along the routes leading to it.Following the demonstration, Khemchand Singh visited the injured people receiving treatment at a private hospital in Imphal but did not respond to media queries.The attack triggered demonstrations at several locations in the state capital. Protesters blocked a road at Khurai Lamlong, while a group of women staged a demonstration at Ema Keithel market.Markets and shops across Imphal shut following the incident, as anger grew over the latest attack.Three CRPF personnel were seriously injured in an IED blast in Kakwa Lamdaibung Lampak, near Singjamei police station. The explosion occurred at 11.41pm on Sunday, according to ADGP Lhatoo."In a second incident around 11.41 PM, an IED exploded at Kakwa Lamdaibung Lampak, near Singjamai PS and 3 CRPF personnel were seriously injured and hospitalised at Raj Medicity," he said.Police were pursuing leads in the case."We are pursuing some leads regarding the incident and are confident that we will be able to take action as per law on the culprits," Lhatoo said.The attack on the firewood collectors followed a separate incident in Thoubal district late on Sunday night. Tension erupted between two communities after unidentified persons allegedly pelted stones during a musical night at Khangabok Pali Bazar, under Thoubal police station.Lhatoo said, "In the first incident last night at around 11:20 PM, tension erupted between two communities following a stone-pelting incident by unidentified persons during a musical night at Khangabok Pali Bazar under Thoubal police station."He said the situation subsequently escalated, drawing in communities from Khangabok and Sangakpham."At around 12.40 AM, one individual succumbed to his injuries; these were bullet injuries, at Raj Medicity, while several others were injured," he said.Additional forces, including the Rapid Action Force, CRPF, Assam Rifles and police, were deployed to the area."Additional forces were immediately rushed into the area, including RAF, CRPF, and Assam Rifles and Police and security forces brought the situation under control at around approximately 1:50 AM today morning, 19th of October," Lhatoo said.He added that police were working to identify those responsible and recover illegal weapons."Efforts are on to identify the accused. Witnesses are being located and questioned, and operations are ongoing to also seize the illegal arms in the area," he said.At least 15 houses belonging to the Kuki community were torched in Chassad village in Kamjong district late on Saturday night, officials said on Sunday. Suspected militants allegedly set the houses on fire, forcing several civilians to flee to forest areas and a nearby Army camp.PTI reported that a Kuki civilian was killed and four others sustained bullet injuries when suspected militants attacked the village earlier on Sunday.Deputy chief minister Nemcha Kipgen condemned the violence in Chassad, expressed grief over the death and concern for the injured village leaders and displaced families. She described the burning of houses as an intolerable crime and said she had directed the district administration, state police and security forces to remain vigilant round the clock, protect civilian lives and property, and ensure those responsible were brought to justice.Police said a joint team of the Assam Rifles, Border Security Force and Kamjong Police had been deployed in the affected area to bring the situation under control.In another separate incident at Kamjong district headquarters on Saturday night, three Tangkhul Naga civilians sustained bullet injuries when rival armed groups belonging to another community attacked the village.Lhatoo said security agencies were coordinating to maintain law and order and prevent further escalation."Manipur Police, in close coordination with the CRPF, BSF, Army, Assam Rifles and other sister security agencies, is working continuously to maintain law and order and prevent further escalation," he said.He added that senior police officials were coordinating with stakeholders to restore normalcy and protect residents."All necessary legal and operational measures will be pursued in the strictest manner to identify those responsible and to bring them to justice," he said.The ADGP appealed to residents to remain calm and avoid spreading unverified information."We appeal to the public to remain calm, exercise restraint, and not take the law into their own hands. People are also requested not to believe or circulate unverified information, rumours, or provocative content on social media, as these may aggravate the situation," he said.He urged residents to cooperate with security forces and report suspicious activity to the nearest police station or the central control room.Manipur has witnessed prolonged violence since May 2023. The latest incidents, involving shootings, an IED blast and arson, have renewed concerns over civilian safety and the challenge of restoring normalcy across the state.
Article Summary: Three Meitei villagers were killed and three others injured after unidentified armed militants opened fire on a group collecting firewood in Manipur. It triggered protests in Imphal, where locals placed two of the victims' bodies outside chief minister Y Khemchand Singh's residence. It came amid a series of violent incidents since Sunday night, including a fatal shooting during a clash between two communities in Thoubal district and an improvised explosive device (IED) blast.

Article Title: ‘Spare India from anarchy’: Over 400 Indian-origin students, academics condemn anti-EC protests
Article Text:
Why is India witnessing anti-EC protests

NEW DELHI: More than 400 Indian-origin students, researchers and alumni from universities in 27 countries have issued a joint statement condemning the ongoing protests against the Election Commission of India (ECI), describing them as a “plan to sow seeds of doubt in India’s democracy”.Titled “Spare India from Anarchy”, the statement criticises the protests against the poll body."An unconscionable and devious plan of sowing seeds of doubt in Indian democracy has been hatched by weaponising sub judice matters, which is then amplified on the streets by leaning on anarchist forces, which have historically and philosophically never believed in constitutional form of governance. All in the name of saving democracy," the statement said."We remain amazed at the irony of all. But more importantly, as informed people who have stakes in the future of this country and travel the world identifying as 'Indians,' we are deeply anguished at this state of affairs," it added.The signatories highlighted the resilience of Indian democracy and the role of constitutional institutions, stating: "In the seven decades since independence, Indian democracy has proved its resilience repeatedly.Institutions have flourished, checks and balances have functioned admirably, and peaceful transition of power has remained an enduring hallmark."They lamented that "a frenzy of election denial, relentless questioning of constitutional institutions, and a preference for 'street over Sansad'" had gripped certain quarters."Unfavourable election outcomes have led to questions of procedural integrity. Adverse judgements have provoked unfortunate commentary on judicial independence. Even the most apolitical institution in the country -- the armed forces -- has been gratuitously and unjustly entangled in partisan discourse," the statement read.While acknowledging that dissent was essential to democracy, the signatories said they refused to remain "silent spectators to the subversion of democratic apparatus in its guise".They urged social and political forces to resolve differences through "debate, discussion, dialogue and dissent" within constitutional institutions.The signatories are based in or have studied at universities across 27 countries, including the US, the UK, Canada, Australia, Germany, France, Japan and Singapore.Their academic affiliations include the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, the universities of Oxford and Cambridge, Harvard University, Stanford University and the London School of Economics, among others. The statement clarified that these affiliations did not imply endorsement by the respective universities.The protests come amid opposition parties’ allegations of irregularities in elections and questions over the integrity of electoral processes.Last month, The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions they claimed were taken without their knowledge, including those related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The report triggered protests by opposition parties and citizens’ groups in several parts of the country, particularly in Delhi, with demonstrators demanding the resignation or removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Kumar, who was appointed an election commissioner in 2024 and became CEC in 2025, has repeatedly faced opposition allegations of electoral irregularities and bias in favour of the ruling BJP.
Article Summary: The statement criticises the protests against the poll body. The signatories are based in or have studied at universities across 27 countries. The protests come amid opposition parties’ allegations of irregularities in elections. They lamented that "a frenzy of election denial" had gripped certain quarters.

Article Title: Tiger Shroff shooting: Videos piece together moments before, during and after attack
Article Text:
Tiger Shroff assassination bid: Videos capture gunfire, shooters’ movements and actor rushing injured driver to hospital

Eyewitness recounts how the shooting unfolded

Police form 15 teams to trace assailants

Lawrence Bishnoi gang claims responsibility

MUMBAI: A series of videos has emerged showing the firing incident involving Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai’s Juhu area, including footage capturing the moments when unidentified assailants opened fire at his car and the actor switched seats to take the wheel after his driver was injured.The incident took place around 7 pm on Sunday near Pushpa Narsee Park, also known as Jamnabai Nursery, where Shroff was leaving after attending a birthday party. Seven shots were fired at the vehicle, injuring his driver, Firdaus, and a passerby identified as Umesh Charan.One of the videos circulating on social media captures the firing incident, with three men involved in the attack. Two of the assailants approached the vehicle on foot while a third waited on a motorcycle to facilitate their escape.The attackers opened fire as Shroff’s car was slowly moving out of the venue. The firing took place around 350 metres from Juhu police station.Another video shows Shroff switching seats with his driver after the shooting. A woman can be heard urging the actor to leave the spot, saying, “Jaldi le kar jaao, Tiger”.The actor took control of the vehicle to rush his injured driver to hospital. Shroff and Firdaus were subsequently taken to Nanavati Hospital in Vile Parle for medical attention.The footage provides a glimpse of the immediate aftermath of the firing, as those present at the scene reacted to the incident.Shroff escaped without any bullet injuries, although he sustained minor abrasions from shattered glass. His driver suffered a gunshot wound to his left hand, while Charan sustained bullet injuries to his chest. Both were taken to hospital for treatment.In another purported video that went viral on social media, the gun appears to jam as the shooter attempts to fire the sixth shot. The other shooter then fires two more rounds, taking the total number of shots fired to seven.The Lawrence Bishnoi gang has been linked to claims of responsibility for the shooting through a social media post and a voice note attributed to individuals identifying themselves as Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu. Police are verifying these claims and investigating the motive behind the attack.Also read - 'Apologise to Lawrence Bishnoi': After Tiger Shroff attack, fresh warning to Salman Khan in chilling audio MEanwhile, doctors said Charan was stable but required surgery. Firdaus was also being treated for his gunshot injury.An eyewitness who was present in the area described how the assailants positioned themselves before opening fire at Shroff’s vehicle.Rakesh Kumar, an autorickshaw driver, told ANI that three individuals were involved in the incident. According to his account, one person was on a motorcycle while two others were standing outside, with one near the gate and another positioned slightly ahead of it.Recalling the sequence of events, Kumar said, "I drive a rickshaw here in Mumbai... I arrived around 7:00 PM to take my vehicle out... There were three individuals involved: one was on a motorcycle, while two others were standing outside - one near the gate, and another positioned slightly ahead of it. When the shooting began, one person opened fire from the front, targeting the specific seat where Tiger Shroff was sitting. .. another person, the one near the gate, fired a shot that struck the driver in the hand. It happened around 7:00 PM..."Mumbai Police have formed 15 teams to investigate the shooting and identify those involved. Juhu police and the Mumbai Crime Branch are examining CCTV footage from the area to establish the suspects’ movements and escape route.The three assailants fled towards SV Road and Vile Parle railway station on a motorcycle. Police are also investigating whether Shroff had received any threats before the attack.The motive behind the shooting remains under investigation.Also Read: 'Apologise to Lawrence Bishnoi': After Tiger Shroff attack, fresh warning to Salman Two individuals identifying themselves as Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, and claiming links to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, purportedly took responsibility for the attack through a social media post and a voice note.The message alleged that Shroff had ignored warnings and also threatened people in the film industry who continued to work with actor Salman Khan.Police are verifying the authenticity of the claims and investigating whether the individuals who issued the threats were connected to the shooting. Their claims of responsibility have not been independently established.The incident has prompted concerns over the security of film personalities in Mumbai, following previous firing incidents targeting Salman Khan’s residence and other attacks linked to alleged gang rivalries.Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis spoke to Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven Bharti to seek an update on the investigation and directed the police to take strict action against those responsible.Fadnavis also spoke to Shroff and assured him, “We are all with you. We will trace and apprehend the accused at the earliest.”Police are continuing their investigation to identify the shooters, establish the motive and verify the alleged gang connection.
Article Summary: A series of videos has emerged showing the firing incident involving Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai’s Juhu area. Video captures the moments when unidentified assailants opened fire at his car and the actor switched seats to take the wheel after his driver was injured. Seven shots were fired at the vehicle, injuring his driver, Firdaus, and a passerby identified as Umesh Charan.

Article Title: Manipur violence: CM condemns killing of three civilians, orders tighter security in vulnerable areas

Manipur CM condemns ‘killing of innocent civilians’ as security forces launch combing operation

Combing operation launched, helicopters deployed

NDA MLAs condemn killings

Fresh violence follows deadly clash in Thoubal

Manipur chief minister Y Khemchand Singh on Monday condemned the killing of three civilians by suspected militants in the border area of Imphal East and Kangpokpi districts and directed officials to strengthen security in vulnerable areas of the state.The three victims were among a group of Meitei villagers collecting firewood in a forest when unidentified gunmen opened fire on them, officials said.Three others were injured and three people were reported missing.The attack triggered protests in Imphal, where demonstrators placed two bodies outside the chief minister's residence. Police fired tear gas shells to disperse the protesters.Singh chaired a security review meeting attended by home minister Govindas Konthoujam, chief secretary Rajeev Singh Thakur, security advisor Kuldiep Singh, director general of police Mukesh Singh and senior officers from the Army, Assam Rifles, CRPF, BSF and other security agencies.An official statement said the meeting reviewed the state's overall security situation and discussed the previous day's incident in Thoubal district and the latest attack in Imphal East.The chief minister “strongly condemned the killing of innocent civilians by armed miscreants at Nongshum in Imphal East district”, the statement said.Security forces launched a combing operation in the Sunurok hills of Kangpokpi district following the attack, deploying sniffer dogs and drones to search the area.Helicopters were also being used for surveillance, news agency ANI reported.Additional director general of police (law and order) Lhari Dorjee Lhatoo said unidentified militants opened fire at around 9.40 am on a group of villagers cutting and transporting firewood near Sunurok hills under Sagolmang police station.“Three individuals died in the incident while three more sustained injuries and they are now under medical care,” Lhatoo said.A joint team comprising police, CRPF, CoBRA, Assam Rifles and BSF personnel was conducting the operation, he added. Mobile checkposts had also been established, while security agencies were closely monitoring the situation.“Police, in close coordination with CRPF, BSF, Army, Assam Rifles and other sister security agencies, is working continuously to maintain law and order, and to prevent further escalation,” Lhatoo said.He assured the public that strict action would be taken against those responsible and appealed to people to exercise restraint.Singh later visited the injured at a private hospital and assured them that the state government would cover their medical expenses.The chief minister subsequently chaired a meeting of National Democratic Alliance (NDA) legislators at the chief minister's Secretariat.In a social media post, Singh said the legislators had unanimously condemned the killings and demanded the immediate arrest of those responsible.“The legislators unanimously condemned the killings of three civilians in the strongest terms. They demanded that police and security forces apprehend the perpetrators of the crime immediately,” he said.Protests also erupted at Khwairamband Ima market in Imphal following the attack, with heavy security deployed in the area.The killings came a day after violence in Manipur's Thoubal district left one person dead and several others injured in clashes between two communities.The confrontation reportedly took place during a musical programme at Cherapur in Khangabok.District authorities imposed prohibitory orders in the affected areas, restricting residents from leaving their homes. A few houses and vehicles were also set on fire.The deceased was identified as Laishram Rakesh Singh, who was reportedly struck by a stone during the clashes. Villagers subsequently blocked National Highway 2, demanding justice and action against those involved in his death.In a separate social media post, Singh said he had met representatives of a Joint Action Committee formed over Rakesh's killing.The committee submitted a memorandum raising concerns about the case, and the chief minister assured its members that their demands would be examined and appropriate action taken under the law.
Article Summary: Manipur chief minister Y Khemchand Singh condemns the killing of three civilians by suspected militants. Security forces launch a combing operation in the Sunurok hills of Kangpokpi district following the attack, deploying sniffer dogs and drones to search the area.

NEW DELHI: A special executive magistrate on Monday extended the judicial custody of Cockroach Janata Party leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das by two days.According to their lawyer, their bail surety was rejected due to a reported mismatch in documents. This is absolutely appalling and deeply disturbing. I cannot remember the last time people were kept in preventive custody under such circumstances. We will pursue the matter legally, but this has been hugely disappointing for all of us," he added.CJP leaders Das and Ranka, along with 12 party members, allegedly trespassed into Jantar Mantar, which is no longer a designated protest venue, and obstructed police personnel on duty.The development comes amid allegations by the CJP that the bail proceedings in the case have been deliberately delayed to prevent the release of its two convenors, who were sent to five-day judicial custody on October 13 following a protest at Jantar Mantar.On Sunday, the special executive magistrate, hearing their bail matter, had claimed that unknown persons were threatening him, following which the police registered a non-cognisable report.In a post on X, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had alleged, "The state is deliberately prolonging Ashu and Saurav's illegal arrest by using every dirty trick in the book to delay court proceedings and prevent their release."They have no legal grounds to keep them behind bars, so they are resorting to delaying tactics to keep them there."The CJP also alleged that bail sureties for the release of its leaders had been rejected on "vague" grounds.

NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Monday responded to Congress president and Rajya Sabha LoP Mallikarjun Kharge , who wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagging the “unusual delay” in proroguing the Monsoon Session of Parliament, which ended on August 13 but has yet to be formally prorogued."With regard to your observation that Parliament has not been prorogued even though 64 days have passed since the House was adjourned sine die on August 13, I would like to clarify that there is no constitutional requirement prescribing a specific period within which a House must be prorogued following its adjournment sine die," Rijiju, the parliamentary affairs minister, wrote in his letter to Kharge."The mere fact that a House has not been prorogued during such an interval does not, by itself, give rise to any constitutional or procedural impropriety," he added.The minister also cited several instances of similar delays during the Congress-led UPA government, inclduing once in 2008, when Houses took up to 87 days to be prorogued.Rijiju further addressed Kharge’s claim regarding the Constitutional Amendment Bill on delimitation. He said the government had reached out to the Congress, the principal opposition party, several times but approached other opposition parties after the Congress failed to provide dates for a discussion."I wrote to you on March 16, March 26 and April 12 in this regard. I had also discussed the matter with you personally and sought your support and cooperation. I also met Shri Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, to discuss the issue and seek his cooperation. However, despite repeated requests, the Congress party did not provide dates for discussion, following which the government reached out to other political parties," he wrote.Citing this, Rijiju expressed surprise that the demand for consultation was still being raised repeatedly and called for the opposition's "constructive cooperation" rather than a "repetition" of the "same demand."Underlining the government’s “firm willingness” to hold consultations, Rijiju reiterated its commitment to the basic principles of parliamentary democracy and expressed hope that the Congress would play a “constructive role” and not obstruct “important future legislations."
Article Summary: Kiren Rijiju responded to Congress president and Rajya Sabha LoP Mallikarjun Kharge. Kharge wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagging the “unusual delay’ in proroguing the Monsoon Session of Parliament.

NEW DELHI: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Monday took a swipe at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his prediction that the BJP 's "expiry date" was approaching, calling the remark "laughable" and describing the Congress leader as a "failed product".The exchange followed Rahul's address at a public gathering in Margao, Goa, on Sunday, where he attacked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah and urged voters to give the Congress a full majority in the 2027 Assembly elections."You think about Goa. In Delhi, in a short while, we will deal with Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. You don't need to worry about that. The work is underway; their expiry date is approaching," Rahul, the leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha, had said.Responding in a post on X, Chouhan said, "It's laughable to hear that the product which failed the quality check every single time in its 99 launch attempts is now talking about the BJP's expiry date."In a separate post, the Union minister accused what he called the "regime change gang" of failing to gain public support, arguing that young people, farmers and women continued to trust the country's leadership."The people of the country have faith in a leadership that has raised India's stature before the world, taught the country to move forward with confidence and stands firm in the face of every challenge.India could neither be misled by false narratives nor intimidated by conspiracies or ideas that weakened the country," Chouhan said.He added that the country's honour and the future of its 1.4 billion people remained the government's foremost priorities."Public trust does not depend on any narrative. Article Title: Tiger Shroff assassination bid: Why Mumbai Police can't get custody of Lawrence, Anmol Bishnoi
Article Text:
Tiger Shroff firing: Mumbai, Rajasthan Police arrest 3 accused

Security concerns and court appearances

NEW DELHI: Mumbai on Sunday witnessed another assassination bid linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, this time targeting actor Tiger Shroff. Yet, Mumbai Police cannot secure the custody of either Lawrence Bishnoi or his younger brother and close associate Anmol Bishnoi.A day after the firing incident targeting Jackie Shroff’s son, actor Tiger Shroff, Mumbai Police and Rajasthan Police have arrested three accused in the case. Mumbai Police are now expecting to secure their custody for further interrogation.The city has witnessed several high-profile incidents linked to the gang, including the assassination of NCP leader Baba Siddique, firing outside superstar Salman Khan’s residence and an attack outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty’s home in Juhu.Despite these incidents, Mumbai Police face hurdles in securing the brothers’ physical custody for interrogation in cases registered in the city. Lawrence is currently lodged at Sabarmati Central Jail in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, while Anmol, who was deported from the US in 2025, remains lodged at Delhi’s Tihar Jail.The latest firing incident has again brought the brothers into focus and raised questions over why Mumbai Police cannot take them into custody for interrogation.The primary hurdle is a ministry of home affairs(MHA) order restricting the brothers’ movement from their respective prisons.In August 2023, the MHA issued an order under Section 268 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), preventing Lawrence from being taken out of prison for any purpose. The order was initially valid for a year and was subsequently extended. The restriction was renewed under Section 303 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which replaced the CrPC.Section 268 of the CrPC empowered the government to prevent a prisoner from being removed from jail, overriding orders requiring the prisoner’s production before a court under Section 267. Section 303 of the BNSS provides a similar power to the state or central government, subject to the conditions specified in the law.The restriction has posed a hurdle for Mumbai Police, which has sought Lawrence’s custody in connection with cases registered in the city. In 2024, the crime branch approached the Union home ministry seeking permission to take his custody in connection with the firing outside Salman Khan’s residence.Police later sought his custodial interrogation in the Baba Siddique murder case as well.Lawrence faces multiple cases, including those involving murder, attempted murder, extortion and alleged drug and weapons smuggling, across states including Punjab, Delhi, Gujarat and Maharashtra. He is also in the NIA’s custody-related legal framework in connection with a case probing alleged terror funding to Khalistan supporters.The MHA restriction means that Mumbai Police cannot simply transfer Lawrence from Sabarmati Jail to Mumbai for questioning. Any access to him has to comply with the restrictions in force.The MHA issued a similar order for Anmol on December 5, 2025, barring police and investigating agencies from taking his physical custody for one year. The order requires agencies seeking to interrogate him to do so at Tihar Jail.Anmol was deported from the US in November 2025 and arrested by the NIA. He is a key accused in the Baba Siddique murder case and has also been linked to the firing outside Salman Khan’s residence.The restriction has created a similar hurdle for Mumbai Police in securing his custody for investigations in Maharashtra. Although agencies can seek to question him, they must do so within the limits imposed by the MHA order.Lawrence’s court proceedings have also involved security concerns. After his counsel moved an application citing a threat to his life, a special NIA judge shifted hearings from the regular courthouse to the NIA headquarters.Lawrence has also frequently appeared before the court through videoconferencing.With both brothers lodged in different prisons and subject to MHA restrictions, Mumbai Police face a legal and procedural barrier to bringing them to the city for custodial interrogation.
Article Summary: Lawrence Bishnoi faces multiple cases, including those involving murder, attempted murder, extortion and alleged drug and weapons smuggling, across states including Punjab, Delhi, Gujarat and Maharashtra. He is also in the NIA’s custody-related legal framework in connection with a case probing alleged terror funding to Khalistan supporters. Mumbai Police face a legal and procedural barrier to bringing them to the city for interrogation.

Article Title: Congress’s post-truth politics: Manufacturing distrust, undermining democracy
Article Text:
For nearly seven decades, Congress govts retained executive control over appointment of CEC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Rajnath Singh is the minister of defence, Government of India.

It is said that often truth is the first casualty of war. This is increasingly becoming true of political contests as well, where post-truth politics is emerging as an important dimension of public discourse.In the post-truth scenario, false propaganda, distorted narratives, and emotional appeals devoid of logic often take precedence over objective facts and verifiable evidence. And, reasoned debate gives way to demagoguery.Once largely a subject of academic debates, post-truth has now become a feature of everyday politics. Misinformation campaigns designed to gaslight are increasingly used to not only sway public opinion but also discredit democratic institutions.Allegations are repeated and amplified even when the evidence to substantiate them is conspicuously absent. In this, truth seems to be not merely the first casualty, but it risks becoming the final casualty as well.India’s political discourse is not immune to this post-truth phenomenon. Increasingly, sections of the opposition parties appear to be manufacturing outrage, peddling propaganda and weaponising misinformation to spread anarchy, placing avaricious political goals above national interests.The article does not aim a jeremiad against the opposition nor a claim that constitutional institutions are beyond criticism. Dissent is the lifeblood of democracy. What it is not is a licence to peddle falsehoods. Disagreement is necessary for better policymaking. What it is not is a pass for vindictive and sustained assault on public trust through allegations that crumble under factual scrutiny.The purpose, therefore, is to challenge these falsehoods and restore public trust in constitutional institutions, which has been eroded by the cynical politics of manufactured distrust.This becomes particularly significant when we examine how electoral institutions and processes have been attacked by certain sections of opposition to hide the fact that people are rejecting them again and again.Three issues, in particular, stand out: the recurring allegations of manipulation of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs), the controversy surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and unscrupulous attempts to discredit the Election Commission of India (ECI).First things first, EVMs have repeatedly been subjected to allegations of manipulation by the opposition. The Supreme Court has examined such challenges on multiple occasions. Finally, in 2024, in its ‘Association for Democratic Reforms v. Election Commission of India’, the Supreme Court put to rest all doubts and rejected demands for a return to paper ballots. The Supreme Court observed that repeated challenges based on suspicion and doubt, without cogent material or data, were “execrable and undesirable”. But this could not stop the opposition from repeating the same lies again and again.The controversy surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is another example of how a legally right and administratively justified exercise has been impugned for narrow political interests by some in this post-truth era.In 2025, the Supreme Court in its ‘Association for Democratic Reforms v. Election Commission of India’ judgment, affirmed that the integrity of electoral rolls is foundational to free and fair elections. It described the objective of ensuring the “accuracy, completeness, and integrity of the electoral roll” as “not only legitimate but is integral to the constitutional mandate” entrusted to the Commission.The Court also found that the reasons advanced for the revision bore a “direct and rational nexus” to maintaining a credible electoral process. These observations reinforced a fundamental principle: protecting the right to vote requires not only safeguarding every eligible voter, but also ensuring that electoral rolls remain accurate, complete and reliable.Beyond EVMs and SIR, a sustained campaign has been run to discredit the office of the Chief Election Commissioner, and by extension the institution of the Election Commission of India (ECI).For nearly seven decades, Congress governments retained executive control over the appointment of Chief Election Commissioner. Our government changed this by institutionalising the appointment process through a multi-member Selection Committee that includes the Leader of the Opposition.The record of Congress has been far from inspiring when it comes to respecting the independence of other constitutional institutions as well.In 1951, the then government introduced the First Constitutional Amendment to reverse Supreme Court judgment and curtailed freedom of speech and expression.During the Emergency, constitutional amendments were weaponised to serve the interests of the government. The amendments made the proclamation of Emergency non-justiciable and placed the Prime Minister’s election beyond judicial scrutiny. It also granted sweeping immunity to high constitutional functionaries and curtailed judicial review. The amendment power was turned from an instrument of constitutional reform into a tool for executive aggrandisement.Not only institutions were trampled but human rights of citizens were also violated. Attorney General Niren De, representing the then Union Government, argued in the Supreme Court that even if an innocent person was killed by a police officer acting out of personal enmity, the victim’s family could not seek judicial relief.Now, compare this with how the Constitution has been honoured in the last 12 years under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The 99th Constitutional Amendment Act, passed by a special majority of Parliament, was struck down by the Supreme Court. The verdict was not only respected, but no attempt was made to overturn it through backdoor legislation. This respect for the Constitution and its principles has also guided our approach to some of the most consequential issues facing the nation.The construction of the Ram Mandir began only after the Supreme Court’s judgment. When Article 370 was abrogated and the Supreme Court upheld the decision, many in the opposition still disagreed with the judgment.Even legislative processes and offices have not been spared by the Congress. A no-confidence motion was moved against the Lok Sabha Speaker when he simply asked the Leader of opposition to follow the rules.Post-truth politics has also extended to matters of national security. In 2019, the Congress leader wrongly attributed a slogan to the Supreme Court’s Rafale judgment and later tendered an unconditional apology in contempt proceedings. In August 2025, the Supreme Court again questioned the basis of claims made by Rahul Gandhi regarding the occupation of Indian territory, asking what credible evidence supported them.Respecting differences of opinion has always been an integral part of our democratic ethos. When people raised concerns over the three farm laws passed by Parliament, we not only listened to those concerns but also repealed the laws in the larger public interest.In a democracy, one is free to disagree with a decision. But such disagreements cannot be founded on falsehoods, nor can their purpose be to create disorder and anarchy. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, in his famous speech in the Constituent Assembly, often referred to as the “Grammar of Anarchy,” warned against the dangers of resorting to unconstitutional methods.His message remains profoundly relevant today. Opposition leaders would do well to read this historic speech and understand the crucial distinction between dissent and anarchy in a democracy.We believe that the foundation of a vibrant democracy lies not merely in political equality, but also in economic and social justice. This principle underpins the decisions taken by our government.At the same time, for a stable and mature democracy it is important that dissent and concerns be expressed through legitimate and democratic channels, and resolved through dialogue and mutual understanding rather than by resorting to disorder.The need of the hour is to ensure that neither our democratic institutions nor India’s rise are held hostage to the frustration arising from political defeats. And, at no cost will the nation's progress be allowed to be undermined by those who would rather discredit the system than confront the reasons for their own setbacks.
Article Summary: Once largely a subject of academic debates, post-truth has now become a feature of everyday politics. Misinformation campaigns designed to gaslight are increasingly used to sway public opinion and discredit democratic institutions. For nearly seven decades, Congress govts retained executive control over appointment of CEC.
