Article Title: What if the next US president turns hostile? Netanyahu's answer lies partly in India
Article Text:
Warning of hostile US prez in future, Bibi seeks India alliance

Netanyahu's US dilemma

Rival slams security doctrine

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has warned that a future US president could be hostile towards Israel, calling for new alliances with countries such as India and nations in Latin America to safeguard his country's strategic interests.Netanyahu unveiled his security doctrine on Sunday, nine days before Israel's October 27 election, arguing that Israel must prepare for a possible shift in Washington's approach. His remarks came hours before US President Donald Trump publicly endorsed his re-election bid."In two years, a President, man or woman, could come to power who is very hostile to Israel," Netanyahu said."How would you deal with that? How would you operate in relation to the United States? And beyond that, what solutions would be necessary?", he questioned.The Israeli premier stressed that his government must make the most of the remaining years of Trump's presidency while preparing for an uncertain political future in the US."First, we must do everything we can during these two years, and during the following two years, in the American arena, through good times and bad," he said.Netanyahu also called for Israel to broaden its network of international partners, pointing to India as a key ally beyond the US."The second thing is to create other alliances. That is what I am working on now with many countries in our region and outside it. India is not a small country, and there are many others," the Israeli Prime Minister emphasised.He also pointed to shifting political dynamics in Latin America as an opportunity to expand Israel's diplomatic reach."There is a major shift in Latin America, and there could be an enormous change in Brazil in just a few days," Netanyahu said, adding, "We must expand our pool of alliances and develop capabilities that make us valuable to everyone."Netanyahu has repeatedly cited his relationship with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and India's ties with Israel to counter perceptions that his country is becoming diplomatically isolated.In May this year, amid a prolonged war and growing international criticism, he described the relationship with India as "unique", calling the country a "huge power" where there is "crazy love" for Israel.Netanyahu's warning comes amid concerns in Israel over declining support among Democrats in the US. Analysts have attributed some of the strain to his strained relations with Democratic presidents Barack Obama and Joe Biden.Those tensions have also featured in Netanyahu's political messaging. He has presented his willingness to challenge American presidents as a sign of a strong leader prepared to defend Israel's interests, a strategy analysts believe has helped him politically over the years.Netanyahu is Israel's longest-serving prime minister.Netanyahu's presentation drew sharp criticism from Gadi Eisenkot, his main challenger in the upcoming election. The former Israel Defence Forces chief dismissed the announcement as a political exercise that offered little substance as the country continued to face security challenges."Nine days before the election and three years after the gravest failure and disaster in Israel's history, with every war front still open, Netanyahu decided to present his 'security doctrine' to the public," Eisenkot said."Two hollow pages, full of slogans that have nothing whatsoever to do with a security doctrine, reveal more than anything the strategic vacuum Netanyahu has left the State of Israel in and his disregard for the security of Israeli citizens," he said.Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of using fear and political messaging to influence voters ahead of the election."This is Netanyahu's method: manipulating perceptions, frightening people and trying to divert attention from the parade of lies and racism surrounding his campaign tonight," he said.
Article Summary: Netanyahu calls for new alliances with countries such as India and nations in Latin America to safeguard Israel's strategic interests. His remarks came hours before US President Donald Trump publicly endorsed his re-election bid. Netanyahu's presentation drew sharp criticism from Gadi Eisenkot, his main challenger in the upcoming election.

Article Title: A 52-year-old Oregon farmer started building miniature castles from rocks cleared off his land in 1935, turning a winter hobby into a four-acre garden of stone bridges, churches and landmarks
Article Text:
AI Generated

How Danish immigrant began building Petersen Rock Garden at age 52

The stonework that put Petersen Rock Garden on the map

PC: Petersen Rock Garden

The miniature landmarks attract visitors

New owners took steps to restore the historic garden and museum

A historic attraction enters a new chapter

In central Oregon, a collection of ordinary stones became the raw material for an unusual roadside attraction. Rasmus Petersen, a Danish immigrant who had spent much of his life farming near Redmond, started arranging rocks into miniature buildings during the winter of 1935, according to Petersen Rock Garden, Museum and Peacock Sanctuary. He was 52, and what began as a seasonal pastime gradually spread across the land around his home. Small castles, churches, bridges and other structures took shape from stones gathered in the surrounding region, with ponds and planted areas added to the setting. The result became Petersen Rock Garden, a four-acre site that drew thousands of visitors during its early years and remains a recognised part of the area's history.Petersen arrived in Oregon in 1905, settling first in Junction City before claiming an 80-acre homestead near Redmond the following year. The land was acquired under the Desert Land Act, a federal scheme intended to encourage settlement and irrigation in arid parts of the American West. Farming became his livelihood, and by the 1920s he had expanded his agricultural holdings to 256 acres, growing hay and grain and keeping livestock.The Great Depression brought difficult conditions for farmers across the country. Petersen adapted by turning to potatoes, but it was away from the demands of agricultural work that he began developing a different kind of project. Reportedly, in 1935, at the age of 52, he started using the colder months to build small structures from rocks cleared from his land. What he made with them would eventually draw attention well beyond his immediate neighbours.The stones were not simply building material. Petersen incorporated local agate, jasper, obsidian and other varieties into his miniature constructions, selecting pieces for their shapes, colours and textures. Bridges linked sections of the garden, while castles, churches and monuments gave the site the appearance of a small settlement assembled from the geology of the region.The work grew over time. Water features, fountains, mosses and flowers became part of the surroundings, adding living elements to the carefully arranged stonework. Petersen also collected stones from within roughly 85 miles of his home, according to the garden's historical account. That broad geographical reach meant the site reflected the variety of material found across central Oregon rather than relying entirely on rocks from a single field.Visitors began arriving while the garden was still developing. By 1938, the attraction had reportedly welcomed more than 7,000 people. What had started as something to occupy the winter months was becoming a destination in its own right.Petersen Rock Garden eventually covered four acres, with its stone creations arranged among landscaped areas and water. Its appeal lay partly in the contrast between the scale of the structures and the work required to assemble them. Buildings and bridges were made from individual stones, placed together to suggest larger architectural forms in miniature.The site also expanded beyond the garden itself. Historical accounts describe a museum, a diner and a pond with islands among its features. Reportedly, by the early 1950s, annual attendance was said to have reached around 120,000 visitors, placing the garden among the roadside attractions that drew travellers exploring Oregon.One plaque on the property sits beneath a miniature Statue of Liberty. It carries the inscription, “Enjoy yourself. It is later than you think.” The wording offers a small glimpse into the garden's character, although its buildings and collections remain the more substantial record of Petersen's years of work.Petersen devoted himself to the project until his death in 1952. His wife, Nyleta Harris, whom he had married in 1950, continued managing the property until she died in 1987. The garden then passed into the care of her daughter, Adele Hegardt, and her husband, Harry. Following Adele's death, her daughter Susan Caward took on responsibility for the site.The stone structures, planted areas and water features all formed part of a landscape that had developed over decades, rather than a conventional museum collection that could be preserved indoors. In 2010, an Oregon family purchased the site, with preservation efforts organised through a nonprofit established to support the garden, museum and peacock sanctuary. The aim was to protect the attraction and restore features associated with its earlier years. A museum refurbishment followed in 2022 after a grant secured through local business Webfoot Home Improvements.More recent efforts have focused on bringing people back into the work of caring for the garden. Since 2022, Marci Wayman has been associated with new ownership and plans to develop the landmark as a community-stewarded nonprofit. Volunteers have helped with restoration and upkeep, while organisers have sought wider participation in deciding how the property should be preserved and used.The garden's future now depends on more than the stonework Petersen left behind. Its museum, landscape and other features need attention if they are to remain accessible, and community involvement has become part of that process. The original structures still connect the site to the farmer who began building them in 1935, long before the garden became a familiar stop for visitors travelling through central Oregon.
Article Summary: Danish immigrant Rasmus Petersen began building Petersen Rock Garden in 1935. The four-acre site drew thousands of visitors during its early years. New owners have taken steps to restore the historic garden and museum. The aim is to protect the features associated with its earlier years.

Article Title: Kim Jong Un photos released to dismiss rumours of coma, takeover by sister
Article Text:
Kim Jong Un inspects pink shoe, women’s coats as death rumours grip North Korea

How the death rumours began

Claims of Chinese troop deployment

What is known about Kim's health?

North Korean supreme leader Kim Jong Un has resurfaced in photographs released by state media, inspecting children's footwear and women's clothing, after unverified claims circulated online that he had died from a brain haemorrhage.The photographs, published by North Korea's official media on Monday, show Kim examining footwear, gesturing towards officials and inspecting coats at a garment and footwear exhibition. The images emerged amid a wave of social media speculation about the 42-year-old leader's health and the possibility of a succession crisis in the secretive country, the New York Post reported.According to North Korea's official Korean Central News Agency, Kim toured the exhibition on Monday. However, the photographs have not been independently authenticated, and it remains unclear precisely when they were taken.One image shows Kim bending forward to inspect a small pink shoe held by a woman. In another, he gestures with his arms outstretched as he appears to address an official. A third photograph captures him reaching towards the sleeve of a woman's coat displayed on a mannequin.The speculation gathered pace after Wanjun Xie, a US-based Chinese dissident associated with the China Democracy Party, posted a series of claims on X alleging that Kim had died and that his sister, Kim Yo Jong , had taken control of the country.In a post on Monday, Xie wrote: "Rumours of the death of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un have been circulating online for days, but Kim Jong Un has not yet made a public appearance to deny them. This indirectly confirms that the rumours of Kim Jong Un's death are likely true. Furthermore, it is rumoured that after Kim Jong-un's death, the North Korean regime has not been transferred to his daughter Kim Ju-ae, but is currently in the hands of his sister Kim Yo-jong."After assuming power, Kim Yo-jong immediately activated loudspeaker broadcasts to South Korea and fired 201 warning shots. She also warned South Korea that North Korea was considering a comprehensive upgrade of its tactical strike capabilities. This sudden intensification of threats against South Korea is clearly aimed at strengthening her control over the North Korean military and consolidating her power through strong external threats. This indirectly confirms the rumors that Kim Jong-un is dead and that Kim Yo-jong is currently in control of the regime; these rumors are likely true."The New York Post reported that Xie's claims began gaining traction on Sunday. However, the allegations have not been supported by medical records, identifiable witnesses or other independently verifiable evidence.In another post on Sunday, Xie claimed that Kim had suffered a severe cerebral haemorrhage, fallen into a coma and been transferred to Beijing for emergency treatment. He alleged that a team of specialists from Peking Union Medical College Hospital had travelled to North Korea before Kim was moved to China."It is rumoured that recently, Kim Jong-un, General Secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea and Supreme Leader of North Korea, suffered a severe cerebral haemorrhage and fell into a coma. Although a team of medical experts from Peking Union Medical College Hospital was dispatched to North Korea to assist in his treatment, the poor medical conditions in North Korea forced Kim Jong-un to be transferred to Peking Union Medical College Hospital for emergency treatment. However, due to the severity of his condition and the fact that the optimal window for treatment had passed, Kim Jong-un succumbed to his injuries and died. His body has been secretly transported back to North Korea, and the news of his death is being kept under wraps."Xie further alleged that Kim's body had been secretly returned to North Korea and that authorities were concealing news of his death. He also claimed that Chinese troops had been deployed to Pyongyang amid fears of a succession crisis.In a separate post, he wrote: "It is said that on October 17, Peking Union Medical College Hospital dispatched a team of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular medical experts to North Korea to participate in the rescue of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, who was in critical condition."Xie's posts also fuelled speculation about a possible power struggle involving Kim's daughter, Kim Ju-ae, and his sister, Kim Yo Jong. He claimed that China had sent 9,000 troops to Pyongyang to help stabilise the situation.The claims of Kim's death, a Chinese troop deployment and a possible succession crisis remain unverified. North Korean authorities have not explicitly addressed the death reports.Kim's health has long been the subject of international speculation. The New York Post reported that South Korea's National Intelligence Service told lawmakers on September 30 that Kim weighed approximately 140 kilograms (309 pounds) and faced an elevated risk of cardiovascular disease because of severe obesity.However, the agency reportedly detected no significant signs of ill health, pointing to Kim's ability to run up stairs during an inspection of a naval destroyer.The latest rumours echo a false alarm in 2020, when Ji Seong-ho, a North Korean defector who later became a South Korean lawmaker, claimed he was "99%" certain that Kim had died following cardiovascular surgery. Kim subsequently appeared in public, and Ji apologised for making the erroneous claim.The New York Post said it had sought comment from the governments of North Korea and China, as well as Peking Union Medical College Hospital.
Article Summary: North Korean supreme leader Kim Jong Un has resurfaced in photographs released by state media. The images emerged amid a wave of social media speculation about the 42-year-old leader's health and the possibility of a succession crisis. Unverified claims circulated online that he had died from a brain haemorrhage.

Article Title: How row over rent turned deadly for Bengaluru advocate: 'One gave cash, another pumped bullet into his head'
Article Text:
According to the police complaint lodged by Manjunath’s brother Muniraju, the advocate reprimanded the tenants over the pending rent.

Unpaid rent leads to confrontation

One tenant hands over cash, the other allegedly opens fire

Police probe source of illegal firearm

Advocates’ association seeks speedy investigation

Killing follows shooting over business dispute





BENGALURU: A 42-year-old advocate was shot dead at his residence in Pattandur Agrahara, Whitefield, late Sunday night, allegedly by two tenants working as delivery agents following a dispute over unpaid rent.The suspects, identified as Pankaj Dube and Amit Kumar Dube, both from Bihar, had been living in a small room behind the house of B Manjunath for around one-and-a-half years. Police said the duo had not paid rent for three months.According to the police complaint lodged by Manjunath’s brother Muniraju, the advocate reprimanded the tenants over the pending rent on Sunday night. The confrontation is suspected to have led to the murder.“First, they came near the house and spoke to Manjunath for some time. Saying they would return with the money, they went back. Around 11.45pm, one of them returned and called Manjunath out,” Muniraju said.A close relative, Akshay, said one of the suspects handed over the rent to Manjunath. As the advocate counted the cash, the other suspect allegedly approached him from behind and shot him in the head.Manjunath was rushed to hospital, where doctors declared him dead despite attempts to revive him.He is survived by his wife and two minor children.Deputy commissioner of police (Whitefield) Saiduly Adavat said police launched a manhunt for the suspects, who allegedly fled on separate motorcycles.Another senior police officer said investigators had leads on the suspects’ whereabouts and were probing how they obtained the firearm.A senior officer expressed concern over the alleged use of an illegal pistol in the killing. Police will investigate where the weapon was purchased and whether the suspects’ associates or relatives possess other illegal firearms, the officer said.Manjunath’s family has four siblings, and the family’s ancestral properties include extensive landholdings and buildings, police said.Condemning the killing, Advocates’ Association Bengaluru president Subba Reddy said representatives of the organisation met police commissioner Seemanth Kumar Singh and sought a speedy investigation.The association also discussed the need for guidelines for private firms hiring workers from other states and for house owners renting accommodation to them, he said.Manjunath’s neighbour Siddegowda expressed shock over the incident and called for measures to prevent similar attacks.The murder comes a week after a realtor allegedly shot and injured his former car driver near Konanakunte over a business dispute. The realtor allegedly fired a round into the driver’s leg using his licensed revolver. Police arrested him and seized the weapon. The driver is recovering in hospital.
Article Summary: B Manjunath, 42, shot dead at his residence in Pattandur Agrahara, Whitefield, late Sunday night. Allegedly by two tenants working as delivery agents following a dispute over unpaid rent. Police launched a manhunt for the suspects, who allegedly fled on separate motorcycles.

Article Title: 'Paris is going to be a Muslim city very soon': Trump slams Macron as riots spiral
Article Text:
At least 2,400 people were arrested, while authorities estimated that around 3,000 businesses had been damaged or looted

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the primary focus for France to resolve the ongoing unrest? Strengthening law and order Reviewing immigration policies Promoting social integration and harmony 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

US President Donald Trump has slammed French President Emmanuel Macron over the escalating unrest in France, claiming that “Paris is going to be a Muslim city very soon” and blaming immigration for the violence that has swept across the country.“Paris is going to be a Muslim city very soon, and that wasn't the deal... Emmanuel should've closed his borders a long time ago. I told him to do it,” Trump said.“The France thing is a very sad situation... What's happening in France has to do with immigration — not schools, not anything — it's immigration. I told President Macron, 'Close up your borders!'” he added.Trump's remarks came as French authorities tightened security following a weekend of rioting that targeted city halls, public buildings and businesses across the country. At least 2,400 people were arrested, while authorities estimated that around 3,000 businesses had been damaged or looted.Also Read: Partial curfews in France as govt battles unrest; PM Lecornu doesn’t rule out ‘imposing emergency’ Paris police imposed an overnight curfew from 11pm on Monday until 6am on Tuesday in two areas of the capital, including Place de la République and the Les Halles shopping district. Demonstrations and gatherings were also banned from 8pm. Several other cities introduced restrictions, including overnight curfews for minors.Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu defended the police response, saying that despite scenes of severe violence and extensive property damage, “no one was killed, and that is a miracle”.The unrest also triggered a political crisis, with Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez offering his resignation on Sunday. However, Macron rejected it, citing the need for continued leadership of law enforcement amid the violence.Macron directed Nuñez to ensure transparency over failures in planning and intelligence-gathering and called for new policing tactics to be introduced quickly.Also Read: Albanian PM warns of ‘red line’ after police station set ablaze Nuñez acknowledged that authorities had “lost control” in some major cities, admitting that the scale of the destruction had exposed serious shortcomings in the response.Meanwhile, far-right National Rally president Jordan Bardella accused the government and Macron of failing to protect the French public, urging voters to use their electoral power to hold the leadership accountable.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has slammed French President Emmanuel Macron over the escalating unrest in France. Trump claimed that “Paris is going to be a Muslim city very soon” and blamed immigration for the violence that has swept across the country. At least 2,400 people were arrested, while authorities estimated that around 3,000 businesses had been damaged or looted.

Article Title: Foreigner alleges rape by man she met online in Goa
Article Text:
The survivor, a divorcee, is European and had subsequently acquired another country’s nationality.

(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)





PANAJI: Goa police have registered an FIR against a man for allegedly raping a 45-year-old foreign tourist at the coastal village of Mandrem.Police said the survivor got in touch with the accused on social media and made plans to meet in Goa.The survivor, a divorcee, is European and had subsequently acquired another country’s nationality. She arrived in New Delhi in Aug before travelling to Goa and has been staying at Mandrem, police said.The survivor, in her complaint, said that she met the accused at the beach and later went to a room, where they consumed alcohol. Police said that as the woman was under the influence of alcohol, she could not resist when the accused person sexually assaulted her.Police said the incident was initially reported at Mandrem police station, but subsequently shifted to the women police station in Panaji, as there was no proper coordination between Mandrem police and the survivor.Goa police statistics reveal that on average, the state sees four women raped or sexually assaulted every week. From 2021 to 2025, a total of 922 women—aged between five and 70—were either raped or sexually assaulted.Police said that higher reporting and registration of offences in Goa reflect greater public awareness, easier access to police mechanisms, and increased public confidence in approaching law enforcement agencies.
Article Summary: Goa police have registered an FIR against a man for allegedly raping a 45-year- old foreign tourist at the coastal village of Mandrem. The survivor, a divorcee, is European and had subsequently acquired another country’s nationality. She arrived in New Delhi in Aug before travelling to Goa and has been staying at Mandrem, police said.

Article Title: Lucknow Police double reward for information on absconding model Shraddha Dubey to Rs 50,000
Article Text:
Police have doubled the reward for information leading to Dubey’s arrest from 25,000 to 50,000.





LUCKNOW: Shraddha Dubey, the prime accused in the death of 28-year-old Shiva Sharma , surfaced publicly for the first time in a brief video interview on Sunday, denying allegations of murder even as she remained untraceable to Lucknow Police, who say they are pursuing multiple leads including a suspected Nepal link.Her appearance came amid speculation that she would surrender at Hazratganj police station, a development that did not materialise. Instead, Dubey spoke to a news agency from an undisclosed location in a video lasting three minutes and 56 seconds, disputing the accusation that she and others were involved in Sharma’s death.Police have doubled the reward for information leading to Dubey’s arrest from ₹25,000 to ₹50,000. Her current location has not been officially confirmed, and investigators have not said whether the interview yielded actionable information about her whereabouts. In a parallel move, Hazratganj SHO Vikram Singh was removed and sent to the reserve police lines.In the interview, Dubey claimed Sharma died by suicide after jumping from the fourth floor of her building. She questioned why CCTV footage from the premises had not been released, arguing that it could clarify the sequence of events.Police have not responded publicly to her remarks about the CCTV recordings, and the footage has not been made public.Earlier, DCP Central Vikrant Vir said police teams were working to trace the accused and were close to locating them, but declined to share operational details, citing the risk of information reaching those being sought. Police sources said Dubey’s suspected location was traced to Mahimnagar in Nepal and that three teams were sent across the border to pursue leads. A 16-member team has also been involved in the search, with investigators suspecting Dubey, her sister Rashmi, and their driver were frequently changing locations to evade arrest.An SUV registered in Dubey’s name was earlier found abandoned near Rupaidiha, close to the India-Nepal border, strengthening suspicions she may have travelled in that direction. Police, however, have not publicly established her movements after the vehicle’s recovery.Sharma died on Oct 9 after falling from the fourth floor of a building near Ballu Adda in Lucknow’s Hazratganj area. His mother, Rachna Sharma, accused Dubey and others of involvement, following which a case was registered under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Dubey rejected claims made by Sharma’s mother and denied that a diary had revealed incriminating details. She also objected to photographs of her with different people circulating on social media and said her sister had no knowledge of the incident.Dubey said she had known Sharma for about four months and claimed he was under financial stress, with debts of ₹16-17 lakh and creditors calling him. She alleged he took jewellery worth ₹5-6 lakh from her residence about a month before his death and promised in a video to return it. These assertions have not been independently verified.Explaining why she left while Sharma was being taken to hospital, Dubey said she had breathing difficulties and personal reasons, and claimed her driver fled after being assaulted. She appealed for a fair investigation, stating no one should be declared guilty before the probe concludes. Police have not confirmed her location or reported her arrest.
Article Summary: Shraddha Dubey, the prime accused in the death of 28-year-old Shiva Sharma, surfaced publicly for the first time in a brief video interview on Sunday. Her appearance came amid speculation that she would surrender at Hazratganj police station, a development that did not materialise. Her current location has not been officially confirmed, and investigators have not said whether the interview yielded actionable information about her whereabouts.

Article Title: ‘Jaldi le kar jaao, Tiger’: Video shows seat switch as Tiger Shroff takes the wheel after attack
Article Text:
Tiger Shroff switched places with his injured driver to expedite his hospital transfer

Lawrence Bishnoi gang claims responsibility for Tiger Shroff attack





MUMBAI: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff reportedly took the wheel and rushed his injured driver to hospital after unidentified assailants opened fire at his car in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday evening.A video of the incident shows the actor switching seats with his driver after the firing. A woman can be heard saying, “Jaldi le kar jaao, Tiger”.Blood stains are also visible in the aftermath of the attack.Shroff’s driver, Firdaus, sustained a gunshot wound to his left hand, while the actor escaped without any bullet injuries. The incident took place near Pushpa Narsee Park, where the actor’s vehicle was targeted by motorcycle-borne assailants.Another person, an autorickshaw driver, was also injured in the firing, according to police.The video shows Shroff moving into the driver's seat after his driver was injured in the shooting. The actor reportedly took charge of the vehicle to get the injured driver medical attention.Shroff and Firdaus were taken to Nanavati Hospital in Vile Parle. Doctors said the actor had sustained minor abrasions but no bullet wounds, while the driver suffered a gunshot injury to his left hand.The other injured person, an autorickshaw driver identified as Chauhan, was taken to Cooper Hospital with bullet injuries to his chest.The firing took place around 7 pm on Sunday near Pushpa Narsee Park in Juhu, when Shroff was returning in his car. Seven shots were fired in all.Unidentified assailants allegedly opened fire at the vehicle, injuring the driver and another person nearby.Police have launched an investigation and formed multiple teams to identify and apprehend those involved. CCTV footage from the area is being examined, while forensic teams have begun analysing evidence collected from the spot.Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, purportedly associated with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, claimed responsibility for the firing in a social media post and a voice note.The message also threatened people in the Mumbai film industry who work with actor Salman Khan.The authenticity of the claims and their alleged connection to the shooting had not been independently established, and police were investigating the motive behind the attack.Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis spoke to Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven Bharti and directed the police to expedite the investigation and take strict action against those responsible. Fadnavis also spoke to Shroff and assured him, “We are all with you. We will trace and apprehend the accused at the earliest.”
Article Summary: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff reportedly took the wheel and rushed his injured driver to hospital. Unidentified assailants opened fire at his car in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday evening. A video of the incident shows the actor switching seats with his driver after the firing.

Article Title: Man stripped, beaten with belts, petrol poured on private parts; video of assault goes viral
Article Text:
(AI image) A disturbing video has surfaced, showing a young man being assaulted in Maharashtra's Latur district.





LATUR: A man was allegedly stripped, beaten with belts, kicked and punched before petrol was poured on his private parts, with the assailants purportedly filming the assault and circulating the video in social media groups. Police in Maharashtra’s Latur district have launched a probe after the footage surfaced, an official said on Sunday.A preliminary inquiry suggests that the incident took place more than two months ago within the jurisdiction of MIDC police station.Police have identified the victim and asked him to come forward to record his statement. He reportedly left the spot after the assault and did not approach the police, the official said.The video purportedly shows the group stripping and assaulting the man before pouring petrol on his private parts. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident and the circulation of the footage.“We have launched a probe after coming across the video. The exact sequence of events and other details are expected to emerge after the victim’s statement is recorded,” the official said.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: A disturbing video has surfaced, showing a young man being assaulted in Maharashtra's Latur district. The video purportedly shows the group stripping and assaulting the man before pouring petrol on his private parts. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident and the circulation of the footage.

Article Title: How Lawrence gang’s ignored call not to work with Salman Khan led to assassination bid on Tiger Shroff: Birthday outing, 350m from Juhu police station, 3 shooters
Article Text:
Actor Tiger Shroff was involved in a shooting incident near Juhu police station after leaving a party

Lawrence gang claims responsibility, threatens Salman Khan's associates

Fadnavis assures actor of support; opposition questions law and order





MUMBAI: Actor Tiger Shroff escaped a firing attack on his car near Juhu police station on Sunday evening after unidentified assailants opened fire as he was leaving a birthday party at Pushpa Narsee Park, also known as Jamnabai Nursery.His driver, Firdaus, sustained a bullet injury to his left hand, while a passerby was also injured in the firing. Despite being hurt, the driver emerged from the vehicle and tried to chase the assailants as they fled.The firing took place around 7pm, barely 350 metres from Juhu police station. According to police, the vehicle was slowly exiting the venue when two assailants, standing amid a crowd of onlookers, stepped in front of the car and opened fire repeatedly.Seven rounds were reportedly fired. At least one bullet pierced the shattered glass of the vehicle's window.The three assailants, reportedly dressed in white shirts, fled towards SV Road and Vile Parle railway station on a motorcycle allegedly kept ready by an accomplice.A video of the incident circulating on social media appears to show one of the shooters struggling to fire when he approaches the car window at close range.Shroff was initially taken to Nanavati Hospital along with his driver. A senior doctor said the actor had suffered minor abrasions from glass fragments, while Firdaus had a foreign body lodged in his left hand following the bullet injury and was likely to require surgery. Deputy Commissioner of Police Mohit Garg later said Shroff had not sustained any gunshot injuries.A third person, identified by police as 35-year-old Umesh Charan, was also injured. According to Dr Chhaya Shinde, dean of BMC-run Cooper Hospital in Juhu, he sustained a bullet wound on the right side of his chest. He was stable but required immediate surgery, a doctor said. A BMC press release stated that he was brought to the hospital's casualty department at 7.10pm with a gunshot wound sustained around 6.30pm in Vile Parle West while covering a football match featuring Shroff.The Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the attack in a social media post and voice note, though police said they were verifying the authenticity of the material. The post, attributed to Bishnoi aide Anil Pandit, named Pandit and Harman Sandhu as those taking responsibility for the attack.The message claimed Shroff had ignored warnings not to work with actor Salman Khan and threatened to target others in the film industry who continued to work with Khan. It also contained threats directed at rival gang members.Sources said the shooters had allegedly been tracking Shroff for several days. Police were seeking details from the actor about any recent threat calls or warnings as part of the investigation.Pandit had earlier claimed responsibility for a shooting outside singer Guru Randhawa's gym in Delhi, allegedly linked to Salman Khan. The latest incident has renewed concerns over threats to members of the film industry, following the 2024 firing outside Khan's Galaxy Apartments in Bandra and the fatal shooting of former Maharashtra minister Baba Siddique in October that year.Juhu police and the Mumbai Crime Branch were examining CCTV footage to identify the assailants and establish their escape route. Fifteen teams were formed to track them down, while a forensic team inspected the scene and the vehicle to collect ballistic evidence and determine the exact number of rounds fired.Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, who also holds the home portfolio, sought details from Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven Bharti and directed the police to expedite the investigation and take strict action against those responsible. He also spoke to Shroff over the phone and assured him that the accused would be traced soon.Deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde visited Shroff's residence late on Sunday to enquire about his well-being. Photographs from the meeting showed the actor with dressings on his shoulder and chest and a bandage on his right arm. Shinde said Shroff had sustained injuries to his hand from gunpowder and glass fragments and assured the family of the government's support.Shinde condemned the firing and said the security of celebrities would be reviewed. He said the government would not tolerate threats or allow gangs to intimidate people.The attack drew criticism from opposition leaders, who questioned the state's law and order situation. Mumbai Congress president Varsha Gaikwad called for a separate home minister, arguing that the chief minister was handling too many portfolios. NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule questioned the progress of the investigation into Siddique's murder and asked why concerns over security remained unresolved.NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar also raised concerns about recent incidents of violence, including the firing outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty's residence, saying such incidents in Mumbai could affect investor confidence. Other opposition leaders accused the government of failing to curb criminal activity and demanded stronger action against the Bishnoi gang.Siddique's son Zeeshan, who has previously raised concerns about threats to his own security, expressed shock over the attack. The incident has once again brought the safety of public figures and ordinary citizens in Mumbai into focus as police continue their investigation.
Article Summary: Lawrence gang claims responsibility, threatens Salman Khan's associates. Fadnavis assures actor of support; opposition questions law and order situation. Shooting took place around 7pm, barely 350 metres from Juhu police station. Unidentified assailants opened fire as he was leaving a birthday party at Pushpa Narsee Park.

Article Title: Sex CDs, honeytraps and power: Why Karnataka politics keeps getting caught on camera
Article Text:
Karnataka has a history of political scandals

What the numbers say

Timeline of Cases

2024 | Prajwal Revanna’s pen-drive scandal- A major political storm broke out after sexually explicit videos allegedly involving former Hassan MP Prajwal Revanna surfaced in 2024. Several women filed complaints, leading to a special investigation team probe. In Aug 2025, a special court convicted Prajwal Revanna in one rape case and sentenced him to life imprisonment. The case remains one of Karnataka's most consequential sexual-abuse controversies.

2021 | Ramesh Jarkiholi’s CD controversy- In March 2021, then water resources minister Ramesh Jarkiholi resigned after a video allegedly showing him with a woman surfaced. A complaint alleged that he had promised the woman a govt job in exchange for sexual favours. Jarkiholi denied wrongdoing and described the controversy as a conspiracy. The episode triggered political protests and demands for an investigation into the allegations.

2019 | Arvind Limbavali’s video- In 2019, a purported video allegedly showing BJP MLA Arvind Limbavali in a compromising situation circulated and triggered a political controversy. Limbavali denied its authenticity and sought an investigation, claiming that he was being targeted. A forensic examination subsequently found the video to be fake.

2016 | HY Meti’s resignation- In 2016, then excise minister HY Meti resigned after a purported video involving him and a woman triggered controversy. Allegations emerged that the woman had sought a favour relating to a job transfer. The woman subsequently withdrew her allegations, and the CID investigation ended without charges being established against Meti.

2014 | SA Ramdas faces allegations- Former minister SA Ramdas faced allegations that he had sought sexual favours from a woman. Police registered a case following a complaint, and the controversy attracted significant attention. Ramdas denied wrongdoing. The Criminal Investigation Department subsequently cleared him of the allegations.

2013 | Raghupathi Bhat’s video row- A purported video allegedly involving BJP MLA Raghupathi Bhat surfaced ahead of the Karnataka Assembly elections. The controversy drew attention because of its timing and the political implications for the legislator. Bhat subsequently withdrew from the electoral contest that year.

2012 | Porn in the house- In 2012, Laxman Savadi, CC Patil and J Krishna Palemar, then ministers in the BJP govt, resigned after Savadi and Patil were caught watching explicit material on a mobile phone during assembly proceedings. A House committee recommended censure of Savadi but cleared the other two. A separate criminal complaint faced a procedural hurdle.

2010 | Hartal Halappa’s rape case- In 2010, then Karnataka minister Hartal Halappa faced allegations that he had raped his friend's wife. He resigned later. The case attracted considerable attention because of his position in the BJP govt. Halappa denied the allegations and faced legal proceedings. A court acquitted him in 2017, citing insufficient evidence.

2007 | Renukacharya’s controversy- BJP legislator Renukacharya faced allegations of sexual harassment from a nurse who claimed that he had pressured her to marry him. The controversy intensified after photographs of the two surfaced publicly. She later withdrew her case, bringing the legal controversy to a close.

Why sex scandals repeat

The flawed ‘honeytrap defence’





BENGALURU: A sleaze CD cost a minister his post in 2021. A trail of pen drives sent a former MP to prison for life in 2025. In between, legislators claimed in the House that dozens of their peers had been caught on camera. For nearly two decades now, Karnataka has seen a string of controversies involving alleged sexual misconduct, intimate recordings and blackmail, often making national headlines.One label has stuck, and the scandals have only grown in visibility and scale. Congress leader K N Rajanna, then cooperation minister, told the assembly in March 2025 that Karnataka was being called a factory of CDs and pen drives. He claimed 48 politicians had been honeytrapped, but named none.The latest allegations, involving political sting operations linked to former CM Siddaramaiah, have revived old questions. Why do such controversies keep surfacing here? Do they point to more sexual misconduct than in other states?Karnataka is often mistaken for the state with the most such cases. But a 2024 analysis of affidavits of 755 sitting MPs and 3,938 MLAs found that 151 had declared cases related to crimes against women, including rape.The analysis, by the Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) and National Election Watch, shows West Bengal had 25 such legislators, Andhra 21 and Odisha 17. Karnataka was not in the top three.An earlier ADR analysis, on a different dataset, placed Karnataka seventh, with seven such legislators. West Bengal led with 26, followed by Maharashtra and Odisha with 14 each. The figures cover declared crimes against women, not necessarily sex scandals, leaked videos or proven misconduct. At the same time, it must be reiterated that a pending case is not proof of guilt.It's arguable from the numbers that what sets Karnataka apart is visibility, not volume. The stakes are high, given the alleged involvement of prominent netas, ministerial exits, police probes, leaked recordings and how often the material becomes a political instrument.There are a few factors that make scandals a recurring theme in Karnataka politics.The first factor is the power imbalance. Legislators control a network of jobs, transfers and favours, potentially leaving those seeking favours vulnerable to exploitation.The Prajwal case, involving videos of women including domestic workers, party staff and govt personnel, highlighted how fear of political influence can delay complaints. The same access can also expose public figures to entrapment when encounters are recorded."When a minister's office controls postings, contracts and licences, consent is difficult to separate from the need to protect one's livelihood," says a retired IAS officer who has worked closely with senior politicians for over two decades.The second factor is rivalry. Compromising material becomes a weapon in struggles within parties, between factions, and between govt and opposition. Allegations involving recordings have repeatedly intersected with contests over ministerial berths, party leadership and electoral prospects.The latest episode has been linked by opposition leaders to a power struggle within the Congress, amid opposition efforts to exploit divisions in the governing party. Some allege the entrapment attempts were politically motivated; others say they were driven by financial blackmail. These remain allegations, not established findings."Their timing often coincides with cabinet expansions and leadership tussles," says political strategist MB Maramkal.The third is technology. A camera in every pocket turns a private act into a recording, and a recording into currency. The Prajwal case showed how explicit material could overshadow an election campaign, trigger police probes and prompt rival claims over who recorded and circulated the videos."Once a file is out, it cannot be recalled. Whoever holds a recording wields leverage even without publishing it. What a man records for control can be copied, leaked or sold by someone else, so the material that traps a victim can also trap the perpetrator," says Vishwanath Belliappa, a software professional.Accused politicians often claim they were "honeytrapped", that is, deliberately lured into a compromising situation by rivals to be blackmailed or disgraced. This honeytrap defence has a corrosive side effect: genuine complaints get dismissed as conspiracy, and real victims become props in a factional fight.Both can be true: a trap can be political, and the conduct it exposes can still be criminal.The law asks what happened, not who gained from the exposure. "No single cause explains the recurrence. The decisive test is whether complaints are investigated impartially, digital evidence is forensically authenticated, victims and witnesses are protected, and allegations are settled through due process rather than political pressure," says Karnataka HC advocate Hidayathullah Kuvendu."Without that, such cases risk becoming political theatre instead of prosecutions, and without reliable comparative data, the state's notoriety may keep growing faster than the evidence to explain it. Karnataka's problem lies elsewhere: its politics treats scandals as ammunition first and crimes second."
Article Summary: Karnataka has a history of political scandals involving alleged sexual misconduct. The latest allegations involving former CM Siddaramaiah, have revived old controversies. Why do such controversies keep surfacing here? Do they point to more sexual misconduct than in other states?

Article Title: 'Apologise to Lawrence Bishnoi': After Tiger Shroff attack, fresh warning to Salman Khan in chilling audio
Article Text:
An audio recording linked to Anil Pandit has emerged, threatening Salman Khan over an apology.





MUMBAI: A chilling audio purportedly featuring Anil Pandit, who claimed responsibility for the firing at actor Tiger Shroff ’s car, has surfaced, with the speaker threatening Bollywood superstar Salman Khan and demanding an apology to jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi and the Bishnoi community.In the audio, shared by the Mumbai Crime Branch, Anil warned Salman Khan against relying on his security and threatened his family if he did not apologise.“Listen to me carefully, Salman Khan. If you don't apologise to my elder brother, Lawrence Bishnoi, or to the Bishnoi community, then we won't even leave a dog in your house. We will destroy your entire family. Keep this in mind. Don't think that you are in security and nothing will happen to you,” Anil Pandit said.The audio surfaced after three motorcycle-borne assailants allegedly opened fire at a BMW carrying Tiger Shroff in Mumbai’s Juhu area around 7pm on Sunday. The actor was leaving Pushpa Narsee Park, also known as Jamnabai Nursery, after attending a birthday gathering when the attackers fired multiple rounds at his vehicle.Two men allegedly opened fire while a third waited on a motorcycle to facilitate their escape.Seven rounds were reportedly fired. Shroff escaped without any gunshot injuries, although he sustained minor abrasions from shattered glass. His driver, Firdaus, suffered a bullet injury to his left hand, while a passerby was also injured.In a social media post, Pandit and another individual, Harman Sandhu, claimed responsibility for the attack, alleging that they had warned Shroff against working with Salman Khan but that he had ignored their warning.“Anyone in the Mumbai film industry who does not listen to us or works with Salman Khan will be next. Wait and watch,” the post read.The message also threatened rival groups allegedly using their name to gain notoriety. Police are verifying the authenticity of the social media post and the claims made in the audio.Mumbai Police have formed 15 teams, including personnel from the Crime Branch, to trace the assailants. Investigators are examining CCTV footage and forensic evidence to establish the sequence of events and identify those involved.
Article Summary: Chilling audio purportedly featuring Anil Pandit has surfaced. Speaker threatens Bollywood superstar Salman Khan over an apology. Pandit claimed responsibility for the firing at actor Tiger Shroff’s car. Three motorcycle-borne assailants allegedly opened fire at a BMW.

Article Title: ‘Lawrence Bishnoi sahab’: Abhijeet Dipke questions Delhi Police’s treatment of gangsters vs protesters, shares old clip
Article Text:
Abhijeet Dipke shared an old video on 'X'





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday shared an old video of a Delhi Police DCP official referring to gangster Lawrence Bishnoi as “Sahab” during a press conference, questioning the police’s treatment of activists and students.“Lawrence Bishnoi Sahab. The respect Delhi Police has for gangsters.Wish they showed even 10% of this courtesy to students and activists who are doing nothing but protest," Dipke said in his post.The video, which dates back to late August 2025, had gone viral at the time and has now resurfaced following a social media post claiming responsibility for a firing incident targeting actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai on Sunday.A message attributed to Anil Pandit, described as an aide of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, claimed that Pandit and Harman Sandhu took responsibility for the shooting. The authenticity of the post is being verified.The message claimed that the actor had previously been contacted and warned, but allegedly ignored the warnings. It also threatened members of the Mumbai film industry, saying those who failed to heed the gang’s demands or continued working with actor Salman Khan could be targeted next.The post also contained threats against rival gang members and hashtags referring to the Lawrence Bishnoi group and its alleged associates.Security agencies and local law enforcement are monitoring social media activity to trace the origin of the message and assess the credibility of the threats against members of the entertainment industry.The resurfacing of the old police video has drawn attention to Dipke’s criticism of the alleged contrast between the treatment of gangsters and that of people protesting peacefully.
Article Summary: Abhijeet Dipke shared an old video of a Delhi Police DCP referring to gangster Lawrence Bishnoi as “Sahab’ The video had gone viral at the time and has now resurfaced following a social media post claiming responsibility for a firing incident targeting actor Tiger Shroff.

Article Title: Another setback for Bittu Tabahi as dustbin installed to keep MP river clean goes missing
Article Text:
Bittu Tabahi says one of two dustbins placed for public use has been stolen

Bittu Tabahi’s Ajnar river cleanup efforts face another setback





BHOPAL: Ajnar river cleanup activist Bittu Tabahi has expressed disappointment after one of the two dustbins he placed along the riverbank to discourage littering was allegedly stolen.The 20-year-old shared a video on Instagram explaining how an initiative meant to help people dispose of waste responsibly had suffered a setback.In the video, Bittu said he had placed two dustbins near the river to encourage visitors to throw their waste in designated containers instead of littering along the banks. However, when he returned to the spot, he found that one of the bins was missing.He clarified that the dustbins were not for his personal use but had been installed for public convenience, with the aim of preventing waste from accumulating along the river and helping keep it clean.Sharing the update on Instagram, Bittu said the drums placed for the convenience of the public had also been stolen, expressing his disappointment over the incident.The missing dustbin incident comes just days after Bittu voiced his frustration in another video over the Ajnar river becoming polluted again despite months of cleanup efforts.His latest update has drawn reactions on social media, with users expressing support for the young activist and disappointment over the reported theft.One user commented, “Bittu support button”, while another wrote, “Zero civics sense India”.A third user expressed sympathy for Bittu’s efforts, writing, “I have started to feel really sorry for him at this point. All his efforts are going to vain, and these people don’t deserve any good!”The incident has once again drawn attention to the challenges of maintaining public cleanliness and sustaining cleanup efforts when waste disposal facilities are allegedly stolen or misused.
Article Summary: Ajnar river cleanup activist Bittu Tabahi has expressed disappointment after one of the two dustbins he placed along the riverbank to discourage littering was allegedly stolen. The 20-year-old shared a video on Instagram explaining how an initiative meant to help people dispose of waste responsibly had suffered a setback.

Article Title: ‘Worried about his future, saddened by 3 deaths’: Mother of accused in Kochi Mini Cooper crash
Article Text:
Image Credit: X (In a video posted on the Instagram page of Iha Design, which she owns, Nooha offered condolences to the bereaved families)

MVD issues show-cause notice to Suhail

Police cite alcohol levels and speed in bail opposition





KOCHI: Nooha, mother of Suhail, the prime accused in the Mini Cooper crash that killed three youngsters at Nedumbassery, has expressed solidarity with the victims' families, saying she understands their grief and that her family will stand by them.In a video posted on the Instagram page of Iha Design, which she owns, Nooha offered condolences to the bereaved families and said the loss of a child was a pain beyond imagination."When we raise our children with so much love, watch them grow up and look forward to their dreams and future, losing them midway is a pain beyond what we can even imagine. I understand that," she said."I am someone who understands the pain a mother or father goes through when they lose a child. I know that none of my words can lessen the immense grief the families are experiencing," she said.Nooha said she and her family would support the victims' families during their time of grief."As a mother and as a member of society, I want to express my support for the family of the three youngsters. My family and I stand by them. As long as we are here, we will continue to support that family," she said.She clarified that her statement was not intended to minimise or compare anyone's suffering, but to express her own helplessness.On the investigation, Nooha said the authorities should be allowed to proceed fairly and establish the truth."Let the investigation take its course and let the law proceed in accordance with the law. I only wish that everything is handled fairly and that only the truth comes out," she said.With the incident being widely discussed on social media, she also appealed to people to show compassion and respect her family's privacy. She said her family comprised four members and urged people not to circulate baseless reports about them."On one side, I am worried about my child's future and what lies ahead for him. At the same time, I am deeply saddened by the loss of the lives of those three youngsters. I do not know how to deal with both these emotions or what I should say or do," she said.Meanwhile, the Motor Vehicles Department (MVD) has issued a show-cause notice to Suhail as part of proceedings to suspend or cancel his driving licence, officials said on Sunday.The notice was issued by the Ernakulam Regional Transport Officer (RTO) following a recommendation from the police investigating the accident. Suhail has been asked to respond within 14 days, after which the department will decide on further action, officials said.MVD officials said they had received a detailed police report recommending cancellation of his licence. Police also found that the Mini Cooper's exhaust system had allegedly been modified, causing excessive noise.Suhail, 19, was allegedly driving the car when it rammed into a scooter carrying three youngsters on the airport road at Nedumbassery in the early hours of October 11. The three victims, including two women, were around 21 years old.Police have also arrested Ninav, Ameer and Joel, who were in the car at the time of the crash.In a report submitted to the Angamaly Judicial First Class Magistrate Court while opposing Suhail's bail plea, police said his blood sample recorded an alcohol concentration of 161 mg per 100 ml, while his urine sample showed 230 mg per 100 ml.The reported blood alcohol concentration was substantially above the permissible limit of 30 mg per 100 ml under Section 185 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.According to the police report, Suhail allegedly drove at more than 100 kmph on a public road while heavily intoxicated, with the other accused accompanying him. The permissible speed limit on the stretch was 60 or 70 kmph, the report said.A court on Saturday dismissed the bail petitions of all four accused.
Article Summary: Nooha, mother of Suhail, has expressed solidarity with the victims' families. She said she understands their grief and that her family will stand by them. Motor Vehicles Department (MVD) has issued a show-cause notice to Suh Hail.

Article Title: Days after quitting BJP, Bollywood singer Jubin Nautiyal’s father Ramsharan joins Congress
Article Text:
Jubin Nautiyal’s father joins Congress

Poll Vote & Share your view What should political parties prioritize to retain their members? Respect and recognition Policy and ideology Member benefits Leadership quality 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





DEHRADUN: Ramsharan Nautiyal, father of Bollywood singer Jubin Nautiyal , joined the Congress on Monday, days after resigning from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), marking his return to the party he had left in 2014.Nautiyal’s move comes months ahead of the 2027 Uttarakhand Assembly elections and after he indicated that a lack of respect was behind his decision to leave the BJP.“I have resigned from the Bharatiya Janata Party. If the BJP president has said that the resignation has not been received, that is possible because I did not go personally to submit it. I sent my stenographer to the office,” Nautiyal had said after the resignation row emerged.He later said he had emailed his resignation to the BJP state president, Mahendra Bhatt, after reading reports that the party had not received it.Explaining his decision to quit the BJP, Nautiyal had said that someone who had been associated with an organisation for 10-12 years would not leave without a reason.“But when a person leaves their place, the main reason should be respected. And if respect is not given, then one will distance oneself. That is what I say,” he had said, adding that Bhatt could explain the reasons for his departure.The BJP had earlier said it had not received his resignation, triggering a brief dispute over whether the letter had been formally submitted.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Ramsharan Nautiyal joined the Congress on Monday, days after resigning from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) His move comes months ahead of the 2027 Uttarakhand Assembly elections and after he indicated that a lack of respect was behind his decision to leave the BJP.
